analysis:
Examined ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler.swift head lines 1-1143 (units 5 and 6). The visible changed lines are: new GLM5NextWiredLimitNotice.report(error, modelID: modelId) calls at line 577 (model-load failure) and line 1023 (stream-start failure), plus the first-content deadline check at ~1147 switching from v2UsageSignal.firstWithheldReasoningAt to firstWithheldOutputAt. Later hunks (~1218, 1325) are outside the supplied text, so they were not examined.

Security-relevant observations: (1) GLM5NextWiredLimitNotice.report receives the raw `error` and modelID. Its implementation is not supplied. The surrounding code deliberately avoids logging raw errors because decoded or template errors can carry prompt fragments (A-001); the other nearby log calls are generic. If report() interpolates error descriptions into logs or user-visible output, that would be a privacy regression. Only model-load and engine-start errors are passed, and it is unverified whether those can contain request content. The modelId is already treated as decrypted-request-derived (comment at lines 464-465 says never reflect it into persistent diagnostics), so report() logging modelID could breach that convention. This is an unverified cross-file contract and needs a check of GLM5NextWiredLimitNotice. (2) The deadline change now treats withheld answer text as generated output, which affects only pre-content deadline enforcement and availability and does not touch the encryption path. Encryption failure handling (emitSSE, lines 823-858) is fail-closed and unchanged (T-008). The cache-receipt, admission and drain flows are unchanged. No concrete regression is established from the supplied evidence. The firstWithheldOutputAt semantics in EngineV2RequestUsageSignal are not visible, so how it interacts with billing floors and deadline correctness is unverified.
